title: Report warns U.S., allies AI chip edge could fade in 5 to 10 years if China keeps getting immersion DUV tools
source_used: Digital Today (Korean, English edition), citing Gigazine
key_facts: The Technology & Statecraft Center says the US and allies' AI chip lead could shrink or vanish in 5 to 10 years if immersion DUV exports to China continue.
It estimates China has secured about 300 DUVi units since 2020, mainly ASML's NXT:1980i.
Continued acquisition could build a base for hundreds of millions of H100-class chips.
It proposes blocking DUVi exports to China in principle and says most licences are approved in practice.
It sees large-scale Chinese domestic lithography by the mid-2030s as unlikely; a Chinese state-owned firm began making DUV tools in July 2026.
If the Netherlands and Japan act passively, the US could use the Foreign Direct Product Rule.
quote_evidence: The report warned that if exports continue as they are, the AI semiconductor advantage of the United States and its allies would "shrink or disappear".
The group estimated that since 2020 China has secured about 300 DUVi units, centered on ASML's NXT:1980i.
The group proposed blocking exports of DUVi to China in principle.
why_it_matters_hint: Pressure to tighten chip-equipment export controls.
notes: Second-hand chain: think tank, Gigazine, Digital Today.
